Okay, so I'm trying to figure out what happens to a wooden log when it's burned. The options are A) It is completely destroyed., B) It is completely changed into heat energy., C) It changes into other types of matter and energy., and D) It physically changes into the gaseous phase.

First, I remember that when wood burns, it undergoes combustion. Combustion is a chemical reaction where wood reacts with oxygen. I think this reaction produces some kind of gases. From what I've heard before, burning wood releases carbon dioxide and water vapor. So, that would be gases. There's also ash left behind, which is a solid residue.

So, if the wood turns into gases and a solid, that means it's changing into different types of matter. The energy released as heat and light is also part of the process, but that's not a type of matter, it's energy. So, the wood isn't just destroyed or turned into energy alone.

Looking at the options, A says it's completely destroyed. But that doesn't seem right because we have products like CO2 and ash. B says it's completely changed into heat energy. That also doesn't fit because the wood isn't just energy; it's also producing gases and solids. D says it physically changes into the gaseous phase, but that's only part of the story because there's also ash and energy released.

So, the best answer seems to be C: It changes into other types of matter and energy. The wood is transformed into CO2, H2O, ash, and energy. That covers both matter and energy, making it the most accurate choice.
</think>
